title: DirtyFileGuard singleton is shared across forked agents
evidence: fork() calls get_guard().recapture() which mutates the module-level singleton. Forked child agents and the parent share the same guard reference, so recapture in a fork affects the parent's guard.
why_it_matters: Child/fleet sessions need independent guard baselines to track per-session dirty file snapshots. Without this, a fork child recapturing its dirty state corrupts the parent's protected file list.
best_practice_anchor: Session-scoped mutable state should not be shared across forked runtimes. Each session should own its DirtyFileGuard instance.
recommended_action: Introduce per-session DirtyFileGuard instances or a GuardRegistry keyed by session_id. Replace the module-level singleton with session-scoped guard lifecycle.

title: clear_history() recaptures guard state instead of preserving conversation-only snapshot
evidence: clear_history() calls _reset_session() which calls get_guard().recapture(). A conversation-only reset should not invalidate the dirty file snapshot because no filesystem mutations occurred.
why_it_matters: clear_history is a conversation-level operation (trim old messages). Recapturing the guard on conversation reset loses the original dirty file baseline and may allow overwriting protected files that were dirty at mission start.
best_practice_anchor: Conversation lifecycle and runtime lifecycle are separate concerns. Resetting chat history should not reset filesystem guards.
recommended_action: Split clear_history into conversation-only reset (preserves guard snapshot) and full session reset (recaptures guard). Or add a preserve_guard parameter.
unblocks: safe clear_history during long-running sessions with dirty files

title: checkpoint and coordination tools have UNKNOWN determinism and mutation metadata
evidence: test_builtin_tools_have_explicit_metadata fails: checkpoint has ToolDeterminismClass.UNKNOWN and ToolMutationClass.UNKNOWN; coordination has ToolDeterminismClass.UNKNOWN and ToolMutationClass.UNKNOWN. Both tools were added by a parallel agent without completing determinism/mutation classification.
why_it_matters: UNKNOWN metadata breaks the contract that all built-in tools have explicit determinism and mutation classification. This blocks tool-level evidence instrumentation and makes dogfood session analysis unreliable for these tools.
best_practice_anchor: Every built-in tool must have explicit ToolDeterminismClass and ToolMutationClass values per the tool contract coverage test.
recommended_action: Classify checkpoint as deterministic_repo_state + writes_workspace (creates commits). Classify coordination as deterministic_repo_state + writes_workspace (writes coordination store). Update both tool classes with explicit metadata.
suggested_slice: Complete checkpoint and coordination tool metadata

title: search_replace.py has recurring PLR0914 (too many locals) and PLR0915 (too many statements) pressure
evidence: Ruff PLR0914 fires on search_replace.py run() method with >15 local variables. The method handles SEARCH/REPLACE parsing, file I/O, fuzzy matching, block application, and evidence emission in one function. Multiple missions have hit this lint pressure without fixing it.
why_it_matters: PLR0914/PLR0915 indicate functions doing too much in one scope. This makes the tool harder to reason about, test, and safely modify. It also creates merge pressure when multiple agents touch the same large function.
best_practice_anchor: PEP 8 and Ruff PLR0914: extract helper methods for distinct phases. Group related locals into typed dataclasses or small value objects.
recommended_action: Decompose run() into phase helpers: _parse_blocks(), _apply_blocks(), _emit_evidence(). Consider a small SearchReplaceResult value object to group block counts and per-file hashes.
unblocks: reduced merge conflicts on multi-agent work

title: pylint.yml and python-package-conda.yml are stale legacy workflows from mistral-vibe
evidence: pylint.yml runs pylint on Python 3.8-3.10 with pip (no uv, no caching) on every push. python-package-conda.yml runs conda + flake8 on Python 3.10 on every push. Both are completely redundant with ruff in pre-commit (ci.yml). Neither has been meaningfully updated since the mistral-vibe fork.
why_it_matters: Both workflows consume CI minutes on every push, produce duplicate lint output, run against Python versions the project no longer supports (3.8-3.9), and create noise in CI results. They also use pip/conda instead of uv, violating the project's uv-only dependency policy.
best_practice_anchor: CI should have exactly one linter per language. Ruff replaces both pylint and flake8. uv replaces pip and conda for dependency management.
recommended_action: Delete .github/workflows/pylint.yml and .github/workflows/python-package-conda.yml. Update the ci.yml pre-commit job if any coverage is lost (none: ruff covers F, I, E, W, N, UP, ANN, PLR, B, DOC, RUF).
suggested_slice: Stage 1 of CI implementation roadmap: remove stale workflows and add missing Tier 1 gates
resolution: Stale workflows (pylint.yml, python-package-conda.yml) already removed from .github/workflows/. CI surface audit Stage 1 complete.

title: test_validate.py and test_validate_git_state.py contain 19 duplicate/near-duplicate git-state tests
evidence: test_validate.py (lines 1469-1797) contains 19 git-state tests that are exact or near-duplicates of tests in test_validate_git_state.py. Includes 1 exact duplicate (test_collect_git_state_non_repo), 6 near-duplicate dirty policy test pairs, and 5 near-duplicate model/profile tests. The Stage 5 git-state tests were added to test_validate.py first, then test_validate_git_state.py was created as a cleaner dedicated file, but the originals were never removed.
why_it_matters: Duplicated test bodies create maintenance burden: a fix to private helper behavior requires updating assertions in two files. Naming collisions (2 tests with identical names) cause pytest to silently skip the second definition. test_validate.py is oversized (1,797 lines, 127 tests) which reduces readability and increases merge conflict risk.
best_practice_anchor: Each test should exist in exactly one place. When a concern grows large enough for a dedicated file, the original tests should be removed.
recommended_action: Remove 19 git-state tests from test_validate.py (lines 1469-1797). All are fully covered by test_validate_git_state.py. See test-cleanup-roadmap.md Stage 2.
suggested_slice: Stage 2 of test cleanup: validate test consolidation

title: [RESOLVED] test_validate.py duplication cleaned up
evidence: Verified: test_validate.py now has only 1 git-state test (test_collect_git_state_porcelain_sha256, the nonduplicate porcelain hash test). test_validate_git_state.py owns all 36 git-state tests. No duplicate test names between the two files. Finding resolved by prior test cleanup.
best_practice_anchor: Each test in exactly one place — confirmed

title: validate_runner.check_missing_dependency incorrectly blocks multi-word commands like 'git status'
evidence: check_missing_dependency() iterates over ALL argv tokens and checks each one with shutil.which(), treating argument tokens as potential executables. For argv=['git', 'status', '--short', '--branch'], it checks shutil.which('status') which returns None, causing the check to be 'blocked' with failure_kind='missing_dependency'. Only the first argv token (or uv+run pattern) should be checked as an executable.
why_it_matters: The quick profile is the most basic validation profile. It runs only git status. Due to this bug, the quick profile is effectively broken in environments where 'git status' needs to be validated. All multi-word commands are silently blocked unless they start with 'uv run'.
best_practice_anchor: Dependency checking should only inspect the first non-flag, non-runner token in argv, not every token. The function already handles 'uv run' correctly by skipping 'run'.
recommended_action: Rewrite check_missing_dependency to skip all tokens after the first executable token is found (or after 'uv run'). Alternatively, only check the first token and handle uv as a special case.
suggested_slice: Fix validate_runner.check_missing_dependency to only check the first executable token
unblocks: quick profile works in temp repos
all multi-word validate commands work correctly

title: AgentLoop is becoming runtime kernel instead of turn controller
evidence: AgentLoop (1852 lines) currently owns or coordinates: conversation topology, context envelope assembly, LLM backend selection, tool scheduling, permission approval, patch gating, telemetry, receipt observation, auto-GC, session lifecycle, middleware handling, connector setup, and teleport integration. Four mixins carry heavy implementation but do not reduce reason-to-change count.
why_it_matters: Every future capability (new guard, new observation, new protocol adapter) will land in AgentLoop because there is no explicit runtime-kernel boundary. The class changes when you modify context policy, provider behavior, tool scheduling, approval UX, telemetry, session storage, GC policy, connector registration, patch gating, or middleware.
best_practice_anchor: Single Responsibility Principle: a class should have one reason to change. AgentLoop has at least 10 independent reasons.
recommended_action: Define a ToolRuntime boundary and extract the governed tool execution pipeline as a first-class object. AgentLoop should retain turn topology and session-level control. Do not split files just to reduce line count.

title: Core AgentLoop imports script-level artifact GC implementation
evidence: AgentLoop._maybe_auto_gc() contains dead code (lines 1288-1330) that imports from scripts.rig_relay_gc_artifacts import run_gc. Additionally, the active GC path at _maybe_auto_gc() reads compute_storage_summary() result incorrectly — treating the dict as a string, so the GC condition budget_status in {'warn', 'over_budget', 'fleet_blocked'} is always False. Both the dead code and the bug were fixed in this session. [UPDATED 2026-05-14: All GC business logic moved to rig_relay/evidence/artifact_gc.py. Script is now a thin CLI wrapper (129 lines, imports from package). AgentLoop imports from storage_lifecycle which delegates to artifact_gc. Zero scripts/ imports in rig_relay/core/.]
why_it_matters: Core runtime importing from scripts/ is backwards: scripts should call core modules, not the reverse. The dead code was unreachable after a return statement. The active path had a type bug that made GC never trigger.
best_practice_anchor: Dependency inversion: core package should not depend on scripts. Scripts are thin wrappers that import from packages.
recommended_action: Removed dead code block. Fixed budget_status dict-vs-string bug: budget_status is a dict, need budget_status['budget_status'] to get the status string. Moved reusable GC logic to rig_relay/evidence/storage_lifecycle.py.

title: Deferred initialization readiness semantics need explicit test coverage
evidence: AgentLoop supports defer_heavy_init=True with wait_until_ready(). If act() is called before the deferred thread completes, the current behavior is unclear — it may run with a partial tool surface, block until ready, or crash with a structured error. No test covers this ordering.
why_it_matters: Desktop cockpit and ACP both use defer_heavy_init=True. If the agent begins processing a user message before MCP servers and context compiler are ready, it could produce incorrect or confusing results without a clear error.
best_practice_anchor: Async initialization contracts should be explicit about readiness semantics and tested for the race condition where work arrives before init completes.
recommended_action: Add an explicit readiness guard in act() or _conversation_loop() that returns a structured error if called while deferred init is still pending. Test by constructing AgentLoop with defer_heavy_init=True, calling act() immediately, and asserting the behavior.
suggested_slice: Add readiness guard + test for deferred init race

title: Governed tool execution pipeline should become ToolRuntime
evidence: The tool call pipeline currently spans _execute_tool_call (180+ lines), _check_tool_result_cache, _should_execute_tool, _ask_approval, _check_patch_proposal_gating, _handle_tool_response, _capture_model_observation_for_tool_response, and _emit_context_observation. These are spread across AgentLoop and three mixins with no unified ownership.
why_it_matters: Adding a new tool gate, observation, or receipt policy requires touching multiple files. The tool execution domain (permission → cache → gate → execute → normalize → receipt → observe) is a coherent vertical pipeline that should be extracted before more gates are added.
best_practice_anchor: Coherent domain pipelines should have a single owner. Tool execution has a clear pipeline shape: stages with early-exit gates, each producing structured output.
recommended_action: Extract into ToolRuntime with a single execute() method that runs the pipeline and returns a sequence of events. AgentLoop calls ToolRuntime.execute() from _process_one_tool_call.

title: Context compiler test drift: 3 tests blocked after compiler restructure
why_it_matters: RelatedFilesPack and RelevantTestsPack were removed when the context compiler was restructured into ContextCompiler.build_envelope(). The existing tests reference these removed classes. The features (related files, relevant tests) are now internal to build_envelope() and still functional in production, but need updated API-level tests.
best_practice_anchor: PEP 8 + test coverage parity: tests should match production API surface
recommended_slice: Rewrite test_related_files_pack_uses_index and test_relevant_tests_pack_falls_back_without_index to test through ContextCompiler.build_envelope(). Fix symbol_codec manifest test to use correct input directory structure for the updated scanner.
demo_impact: none — demo path uses build_envelope() which works correctly

title: DesktopBridgeServer relies on implicit probe ladder and boolean flag pile
evidence: DesktopBridgeServer.start uses a probe ladder (bridge:01 through bridge:18) and multiple boolean flags to track connection bring-up. Race conditions during token verification and port binding cause frontend connection failures.
why_it_matters: Implicit state makes startup connection failures difficult to debug and leads to race conditions between pywebview window creation and WebSocket binding. A formalized state machine is required to ensure reliable desktop cockpit initialization.
best_practice_anchor: Complex multi-phase initialization workflows should be managed by an explicit state machine rather than callback chains and boolean flags.
recommended_action: Extract DesktopBridgeStateMachine to manage the connection lifecycle with explicit phases and strict transition validation.
suggested_slice: P0 Desktop Bridge State Machine Conversion

title: RuntimeSupervisor.execute relies on implicit while True polling loop
evidence: RuntimeSupervisor.execute contains a complex while True polling loop for heartbeat monitoring and stall detection. Subprocess state transitions are obscured within conditional blocks.
why_it_matters: Implicit polling loops obscure state transitions, increase CPU utilization, and make heartbeat stall recovery difficult to trace and audit.
best_practice_anchor: Subprocess supervision should be event-driven with explicit state transitions and structured OpenTelemetry tracing.
recommended_action: Convert RuntimeSupervisor.execute into an event-driven RuntimeSupervisorStateMachine with explicit stall and recovery transitions.
suggested_slice: P0 Runtime Supervisor State Machine Conversion

title: 92+ Markdown audit/report/roadmap files in docs/audits/ violate canonical JSON artifact policy
evidence: Directory docs/audits/ contains 93 .md files (including release-candidate-convergence-spine.md, telemetry-panopticon-audit.md, test-suite-reality-pressure-audit.md, and 90+ others). The migration manifest at docs/json/documentation_migration_manifest.v1.json currently has 7 entries. Only a few audits have been migrated to docs/json/audits/. The rest remain as Markdown in violation of the canonical structured-report policy.
why_it_matters: Under the AGENTS.md canonical structured-report policy, audits, roadmaps, evidence inventories, and validation ledgers must be JSON, JSONL, or CSV. The 93 Markdown files in docs/audits/ predate this policy and need migration to enable static rendering, schema validation, and structured querying via the analytics substrate.
best_practice_anchor: AGENTS.md documentation policy — canonical JSON artifacts
recommended_action: Migrate docs/audits/*.md to docs/json/audits/*.v1.json over 3 waves: (1) Phase 4-5 release-critical audits, (2) architecture/design audits, (3) historical/closure audits. Each wave updates the migration manifest, validates schemas, and preserves old Markdown until all migration rules are satisfied.
suggested_slice: Migrate docs/audits/ Markdown leaks to canonical JSON over 3 waves

title: Analytics projection and main projection overwrite each other in frontend state
evidence: In projection.js handleProjection(), state.projection is completely overwritten by incoming projection. Since the main projection and analytics projection are distinct websocket payloads with different schemas, they wipe out each other's data, causing all widgets from the other kind to show 'Unavailable'. Additionally, the client never sends analytics_subscribe, and there is no conversion from the backend widgets array structure to the flat camelCase structure expected by the analytics widgets.
why_it_matters: This makes the entire Analytics Data Lake frontend display non-functional; analytics widgets can never render real data alongside the main cockpit widgets.
best_practice_anchor: Frontend state management should isolate distinct data domains (main projection vs analytics data) instead of completely overwriting the root projection state object. Client-server subscription handshakes must be wired.
recommended_action: 1. Isolate analytics state under state.analytics in state.js rather than replacing state.projection. 2. Send analytics_subscribe from client on mode switch to analytics. 3. Map backend widgets array to frontend camelCase keys under state.analytics.
suggested_slice: Fix analytics projection state conflict and subscription wiring
